lesson.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust
lesson.goal: build a command-line tool in Rust with cargo that parses arguments

sources.title: Build a Custom ls CLI Tool in Rust

steps.title: Initialize project and add clap
steps.instructions: Run cargo new bestls && cd bestls in the workdir, then open Cargo.toml. Add clap with the derive feature under [dependencies].

targets.caption: Create a new Cargo binary project
Add clap with the derive feature

explanations.topic: Why clap with derive feature is used for CLI parsing

hints: Run cargo new <name> in your empty working directory first.
Open Cargo.toml and locate the [dependencies] section.
Add clap = { version = "4.5.39", features = ["derive"] } under [dependencies].
common_mistakes: Forgetting to enable features = ["derive"] for clap, which prevents #[derive(Parser)] from compiling.
Running commands outside the newly created project directory.

steps.title: Define CLI struct and run help
steps.instructions: In src/main.rs, define a CLI struct deriving Debug and Parser with an optional path: Option<PathBuf> field, and parse it in main. Run the tool with -h to verify generated help output.

targets.caption: Define the CLI struct with an optional PathBuf

explanations.topic: Passing arguments to cargo run using --
Automatic help generation from clap Parser

hints: Import clap::Parser and std::path::PathBuf at the top of src/main.rs.
Annotate struct CLI with #[derive(Debug, Parser)].
Pass -h after -- when running cargo run so cargo forwards the flag to your binary.
common_mistakes: Running cargo run -h without --, which shows Cargo's own help instead of your program's help.
Forgetting to import clap::Parser or std::path::PathBuf.
steps.code: use clap::Parser; use std::path::PathBuf; #[derive(Debug, Parser)] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); println!("Hello, world!"); }

steps.title: Add command metadata and default path
steps.instructions: Add #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best ls command ever")] to CLI, then unwrap cli.path with a default PathBuf::from(".") and print path.display(). Test --help and passing a custom path argument.

explanations.topic: Defaulting an Option<PathBuf> to the current directory

hints: Place #[command(version, about, long_about = "...")] right above struct CLI.
Use cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")) to default to the current folder.
Format PathBuf for printing using path.display().
common_mistakes: Using println!("{}", path) directly on PathBuf instead of path.display(), which does not implement Display.
Placing #[command(...)] after struct CLI instead of above it.
steps.code: #[derive(Debug, Parser)] #[command(version, about, long_about = "Best ls command ever")] struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, } fn main() { let cli = CLI::parse(); let path = cli.path.unwrap_or(PathBuf::from(".")); println!("{}", path.display()); }

steps.title: Check path existence with colored output
steps.instructions: Add owo-colors = "4.2.1" to Cargo.toml, then check fs::exists(&path) in main and print "Path does not exist".red() when false. Build with cargo build and test a nonexistent path.

explanations.topic: Running the compiled binary directly from target/debug

hints: Import std::fs and owo_colors::OwoColorize in src/main.rs.
fs::exists(&path) returns a Result<bool, io::Error>, so unwrap it with if let Ok(does_exist).
Call .red() on the string literal inside println!("{}", ...).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import owo_colors::OwoColorize, which provides the .red() trait method.
Treating fs::exists(&path) as a plain bool instead of matching Ok(does_exist).
steps.code: use owo_colors::OwoColorize; use std::fs; if let Ok(does_exist) = fs::exists(&path) { if does_exist { } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } }

steps.title: Read and list directory filenames
steps.instructions: Handle the Err case of fs::exists with a red error message, and create fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> using fs::read_dir(path). Loop over get_files(&path) in main to print every entry.

explanations.topic: Why fs::exists returns Result<bool> for unreadable paths

hints: Import std::path::Path alongside PathBuf.
Iterate over entry in read_dir and unwrap each Result with if let Ok(file) = entry.
Convert file.file_name() from OsString using .into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()).
common_mistakes: Passing path by value instead of &path to get_files.
Forgetting to convert file.file_name() (an OsString) into a String.
steps.code: if does_exist { for file in get_files(&path) { println!("{}", file); } } else { println!("{}", "Path does not exist".red()); } } else { println!("{}", "error reading directory".red()); } fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<String> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { data.push(file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into())); } } } data }

steps.title: Extract file metadata into FileEntry
steps.instructions: Add strum and strum_macros (0.27) to Cargo.toml, define EntryType and FileEntry structs, and update get_files and map_data to extract fs::metadata(&file.path()). Run cargo run to inspect the debug output.

explanations.topic: Using strum Display macro on enums

hints: Add both strum = { version = "0.27", features = ["derive"] } and strum_macros = "0.27" to Cargo.toml.
Call fs::metadata(&file.path()), not fs::metadata(&path), so you get each entry's individual size and type.
Use {:?} in println! when printing FileEntry structs.
common_mistakes: Passing the directory &path instead of &file.path() to fs::metadata, causing every entry to show the directory's size and type.
Forgetting to change get_files' return type from Vec<String> to Vec<FileEntry>.
steps.code: use strum::Display; #[derive(Debug, Display)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug)] struct FileEntry { name: String, e_type: EntryType, len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } fn get_files(path: &Path) -> Vec<FileEntry> { let mut data = Vec::default(); if let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(path) { for entry in read_dir { if let Ok(file) = entry { map_data(file, &mut data); } } } data } fn map_data(file: fs::DirEntry, data: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) { if let Ok(meta) = fs::metadata(&file.path()) { data.push(FileEntry { name: file.file_name().into_string().unwrap_or("unknown name".into()), e_type: if meta.is_dir() { EntryType::Dir } else { EntryType::File }, len_btyes: meta.len(), modified: "".to_string(), }); } }

steps.title: Style table output with tabled
steps.instructions: Add tabled = "0.20.0" to Cargo.toml, derive Tabled on FileEntry with #[tabled(rename = ...)] headers, and render a rounded, colorized Table in main. Run cargo run to view the formatted table.

explanations.topic: Rendering structs as ASCII tables with tabled

hints: Import Table, Tabled, Style, Color, Columns, and Rows from tabled.
Make sure you import tabled::settings::Style and tabled::settings::Color, not clap or owo-colors types.
Call table.with(Style::rounded()) and table.modify(...) before println!("{}", table).
common_mistakes: Importing Color or Style from owo_colors or clap instead of tabled::settings.
Forgetting mut on let mut table = Table::new(...) when calling .with() and .modify().
steps.code: use tabled::{settings::{object::{Columns, Rows}, Color, Style}, Table, Tabled}; #[derive(Debug, Tabled)] struct FileEntry { #[tabled(rename="Name")] name: String, #[tabled(rename="Type")] e_type: EntryType, #[tabled(rename="Size B")] len_btyes: u64, modified: String, } let get_files = get_files(&path); let mut table = Table::new(get_files); table.with(Style::rounded()); table.modify(Columns::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_CYAN); table.modify(Columns::one(2), Color::FG_BRIGHT_MAGENTA); table.modify(Rows::first(), Color::FG_BRIGHT_GREEN); println!("{}", table);

steps.title: Format modified dates with chrono
steps.instructions: Add chrono = "0.4.41" to Cargo.toml, convert meta.modified() into DateTime<Utc> formatted as "%a %b %e %Y" in map_data, and update the third column color to FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW. Run cargo run on both . and src.

explanations.topic: Converting SystemTime from meta.modified() using chrono DateTime<Utc>

hints: Import chrono::{DateTime, Utc} in src/main.rs.
Rename the inner variable from mod to modi because mod is a reserved Rust keyword.
Fix the fourth column index in table.modify to Columns::one(3) for FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW.
common_mistakes: Naming the variable mod inside if let Ok(mod) = meta.modified(), which fails because mod is a Rust keyword.
Applying FG_BRIGHT_YELLOW to Columns::one(2) instead of Columns::one(3).
steps.code: use chrono::{DateTime, Utc}; modified: if let Ok(modi) = meta.modified() { let date: DateTime<Utc> = modi.into(); format!("{}", date.format("%a %b %e %Y")) } else { String::default() },

steps.title: Add JSON output flag with serde
steps.instructions: Add a #[arg(short, long)] json: bool field to your CLI struct, add serde (features derive) and serde_json to Cargo.toml, and derive Serialize on EntryType and FileEntry. When cli.json is true print serde_json::to_string(&get_files(&path)), then run cargo run -- -j.

targets.caption: Serialize entries to JSON when -j passed
Run cargo run -- -j and see JSON

explanations.topic: Adding boolean flags with #[arg(short, long)] in clap
Serializing structs and nested enums with serde

hints: Both FileEntry and EntryType must derive Serialize for serde_json::to_string to compile.
Annotate json: bool with #[arg(short, long)] so it acts as a flag rather than a positional argument.
Test both cargo run -- -j and cargo run -- --json.
common_mistakes: Forgetting #[arg(short, long)] on json: bool, which causes clap to panic because a positional bool is invalid.
Deriving Serialize on FileEntry without also deriving Serialize on EntryType.
steps.code: use serde::Serialize; #[derive(Debug, Display, Serialize)] enum EntryType { File, Dir, } #[derive(Debug, Tabled, Serialize)] struct FileEntry { ... } struct CLI { path: Option<PathBuf>, #[arg(short, long)] json: bool, } if cli.json { let get_files = get_files(&path); println!("{}", serde_json::to_string(&get_files).unwrap_or("cannot parse json".to_string())); } else { print_table(path); }
